intro.title: useLocalStorage
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that saves and retrieves a user's name using the browser's local storage. You will learn how to create a custom React hook called useLocalStorage to manage state that persists between page reloads. The main technologies involved are React hooks (useState, useEffect) and the browser's localStorage API. By the end, you'll understand how to implement persistent data in a React application with a reusable custom hook.
intro.usecase: The useLocalStorage pattern appears in countless real-world applications where users expect their preferences and data to persist between sessions. In e-commerce sites, it remembers shopping cart items when users navigate away temporarily. Dashboard applications use it to save user-selected filters, chart configurations, and panel layouts. Form-heavy applications like survey tools or configuration wizards employ it to prevent data loss if users accidentally close their browser, creating a more resilient user experience.
